200: Kashimashi: Girl Meets Girl by Satoru Akahori and Yukimaru Katsura (Seven Seas) is a gentle romantic comedy with a sci-fi twist. Hazumu Osaragi is a shy, kind boy who has just been turned down by his crush, Yasuna. Then an alien spaceship crashes on him, and he wakes up as a girl. Now Hazumu has to relearn daily life while caught between Yasuna and his tomboyish childhood friend Tomari. It's a sweet, funny pick for fans of yuri and love triangles.
203: Record of Grancrest War by Ryo Mizuno and Makoto Yotsuba (Viz Media) is a fantasy war story full of knights, mages and shifting alliances. The continent is torn by Chaos, and the lords who hold the power to calm it are too busy fighting each other. Siluca Meletes, a gifted mage, makes a contract with Theo Cornaro, a wandering knight with a small Crest and a big dream of freeing his homeland. Readers who like strategy and political fantasy will feel at home here.
205: Kyo Kara Maoh! by Tomo Takabayashi and Temari Matsumoto (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. Yuri Shibuya is an ordinary, baseball-loving high schooler until a pack of bullies dunks his head in a toilet and he gets flushed into another world. There he learns he is the new Demon King, expected to rule a kingdom he knows nothing about. Readers who enjoy fish-out-of-water humor and a big cast of handsome retainers will have fun with it.
208: Saikano by Shin Takahashi (Viz Media) is a bittersweet sci-fi romance. Shuji and Chise are high school classmates in a small seaside town, awkwardly figuring out how to be a couple. Then a sudden air raid reveals that clumsy, shy Chise has been turned into the military's ultimate weapon. The story follows two teens trying to hold on to an ordinary love while the world falls into war. It's a good fit for readers who like tender, melancholy stories.
211: Sakura Taisen by Ohji Hiroi and Ikku Masa (Tokyopop) is an action story set in a steam-powered version of 1920s Tokyo. Navy officer Ichiro Ogami expects a combat command, but he's assigned to the Imperial Floral Assault Troupe, a group of young women who perform as a theater company. Secretly, they also pilot steam-driven mecha to defend the city from demons. Fans of the classic Sega games will enjoy seeing the cast on the page.
213: Scott Pilgrim by Bryan Lee O'Malley (Oni Press) is a funny, energetic comic about love, music and video games. Scott is a 23-year-old slacker in Toronto who plays bass in a struggling band. When he falls for Ramona Flowers, a mysterious delivery girl, he learns that to date her, he has to defeat her seven evil exes in battle. It's a great pick for anyone who grew up on video games and indie rock.
216: Love Stage!! by Eiki Eiki and Taishi Zaou (Sublime) is a bright, silly boys' love romantic comedy. Izumi Sena comes from a famous showbiz family, but all he wants is to be a manga artist and enjoy his anime. Years ago he played a bride in a TV commercial, and when the crew reunites for a sequel, rising actor Ryoma learns that the girl he has been pining for is actually a boy. Fans of lighthearted BL will find plenty to laugh at.
217: Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai by Riku Sanjo and Koji Inada (Viz Media) is a classic fantasy adventure. Dai is a boy raised by friendly monsters on a remote island, and he dreams of becoming a great hero. When the Dark King Hadlar returns and the island's monsters turn wild, Dai sets out to train and fight with a growing band of friends. It's a warm, exciting read for fans of the games and old-school shonen action.
220: Mamotte! Lollipop by Michiyo Kikuta (Kodansha) is a cute, bubbly magical romance. Nina is a middle schooler who accidentally swallows the Crystal Pearl, a prize that wizards-in-training need to pass their exam. Suddenly she's a target, and two young wizards, Zero and Ichii, step in to protect her while trying to get the pearl back. It's a fun, light pick for younger shojo readers who like magic and cute boys.
222: Durarara!! by Ryohgo Narita and Akiyo Satorigi (Yen Press) is a stylish urban mystery with a supernatural edge. Mikado Ryugamine moves to Tokyo's Ikebukuro district hoping for a more exciting life. He quickly finds it, along with color gangs, a vending-machine-throwing strongman, an information broker and the city's most famous urban legend: a headless rider on a black motorcycle. Readers who like large casts and interlocking stories will enjoy this one.
223: Fake by Sanami Matoh (Tokyopop) is a boys' love police drama with plenty of humor. Randy "Ryo" MacLean is a new detective at New York's 27th Precinct, and he is partnered with Dee Laytner, a brash cop who makes his interest in Ryo very clear. Between murder cases and street crime, the two slowly figure out what they mean to each other. It's a classic BL series that fans of buddy-cop stories will enjoy.
224: Fighting for Tomorrow (Ashita no Joe) by Asao Takamori and Tetsuya Chiba (Kodansha) is a gritty, classic boxing drama. Joe Yabuki is a reckless young drifter who wanders into Tokyo's slums looking for trouble. Danpei Tange, a washed-up former boxer, sees raw talent in him and is determined to turn him into a champion, if Joe can stay out of trouble long enough. It's a landmark sports manga for anyone who loves underdog stories.
225: Sherlock Bones by Yuma Ando and Yuki Sato (Kodansha) is a lighthearted mystery comedy. High schooler Takeru Wajo adopts a puppy, and soon learns that it's the reincarnation of Sherlock Holmes himself. Takeru is the only one who can understand him, so the pair work together to help Takeru's detective father crack his cases, with Takeru taking the credit. It's a fun, quick read for fans of whodunits and goofy animal sidekicks.
227: Shoulder-a-Coffin Kuro by Satoko Kiyuduki (Yen Press) is a quiet, dreamlike fantasy. Kuro is a traveler dressed all in black who carries a coffin on her back wherever she goes. With her talking bat companion Sen, she wanders from town to town in search of the witch who cursed her, meeting strange and kind people along the way. It's a gentle, melancholy story for readers who like fairy-tale moods and soft art.
229: Yu-Gi-Oh! Millennium World by Kazuki Takahashi (Viz Media) is the action-adventure final arc of the original Yu-Gi-Oh! story. Yugi Mutou and the spirit of the nameless Pharaoh who lives inside the Millennium Puzzle have gathered the clues they need to uncover the Pharaoh's lost past. The journey takes them into his memories of ancient Egypt, where monster battles are real. Fans of the original series will want this to finish the story.
230: Full Moon O Sagashite by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is an emotional shojo fantasy about music and dreams. Twelve-year-old Mitsuki Koyama wants to be a singer, but a tumor in her throat stands in her way. Then two shinigami appear to her, and one of them gives her the power to transform into a healthy sixteen-year-old so she can chase her dream. It's a heartfelt read for fans of magical girls and bittersweet romance.
232: The Executioner and Her Way of Life by Mato Sato and Ryo Mitsuya (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy with a twist on isekai stories. In this world, people summoned from Japan arrive with dangerous powers, and Menou is the executioner sent to quietly kill them. Her newest target, the cheerful Akari, turns out to be far harder to get rid of than any before. Readers who like yuri, assassins and morally gray heroines will enjoy it.
233: Black Bullet by Shiden Kanzaki with illustrations by Saki Ukai (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel series. Humanity survives behind walls that keep out the Gastrea, monsters created by a parasitic virus. Rentaro Satomi is a young Civil Security officer who fights them alongside his partner, Enju, one of the Cursed Children, girls born with powers from the virus. It's a fast, hard-hitting read for fans of dystopian battle stories.
236: Days with My Stepsister by Ghost Mikawa (Seven Seas) is a quiet, grounded romance light novel. When high schooler Yuta Asamura's father remarries, Yuta gains a stepsister his own age, the cool and guarded Saki Ayase. The two agree not to expect too much from each other and to keep things honest, but sharing a home slowly changes how they see one another. It's a thoughtful slow burn for readers who prefer realistic, low-drama romance.
237: Solo Leveling by Chugong (Yen Press) is the original Korean web novel behind the hit action series. Monsters pour into the world through dungeon gates, and hunters with special powers fight them. Sung Jinwoo is known as the world's weakest hunter, until a deadly raid leaves him with a mysterious System that lets him level up like a game character. Fans of the manhwa and anime will enjoy reading the story in its first form.
238: Bungo Stray Dogs by Kafka Asagiri (Yen Press) is a set of light novels that expand on the supernatural detective series. The main story follows Atsushi Nakajima, an orphan who joins the Armed Detective Agency, a team of gifted people named after famous authors. The novels fill in side stories and backstories for the cast, including Dazai's early days. They're a great pick for fans of the manga and anime who want more of these characters.
239: Fullmetal Alchemist by Makoto Inoue (Viz Media) is a series of light novels based on Hiromu Arakawa's fantasy adventure manga. Brothers Edward and Alphonse Elric tried to use alchemy to bring back their mother and paid a terrible price. Now they travel the country searching for the Philosopher's Stone to restore their bodies. These novels tell new standalone adventures from that journey, so they're a nice extra for fans who've finished the manga.
240: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- by Tappei Nagatsuki (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy manga adaptation of the hit light novels. Subaru Natsuki is a shut-in who is suddenly pulled into a fantasy world with no powers at all. He soon learns he has one strange ability: when he dies, time rewinds to an earlier point. He uses it to protect Emilia, the silver-haired girl who helped him. Readers who like tense, emotional isekai will be hooked.
241: Naruto by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) has a set of light novels that add new stories to the beloved ninja series. Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, lonely orphan in the Hidden Leaf Village who dreams of becoming Hokage, the village's strongest ninja. The novels give side characters and later chapters of the Naruto world more room to breathe. They're a nice extra for fans who want more after finishing the manga.
243: Haruka: Beyond the Stream of Time by Tohko Mizuno (Viz Media) is a historical fantasy romance. High schooler Akane Motomiya is pulled into Kyo, a world modeled on Heian-era Japan. There she learns she is the Priestess of the Dragon God, the one person who can save the capital from a demon clan. Eight handsome guardians are sworn to protect her as she learns her new role. Fans of reverse-harem fantasy will enjoy the setting.
245: Tokyo ESP by Hajime Segawa (Vertical) is a superpowered action story set in Tokyo. Rinka Urushiba is a poor but kind high school girl who lives with her father. One night she sees a glowing flying fish, and the next morning she can pass through solid objects. Soon people all over the city are gaining powers, and Rinka must decide what kind of hero she wants to be. It's a fun pick for fans of action with a strong heroine.
246: Mr. Villain's Day Off by Yuu Morikawa (Square Enix Manga) is a cozy slice-of-life comedy. The General is a fearsome commander in an evil organization fighting the local superhero team. On his days off, though, he's a polite guy who loves pandas, tries new snacks and gets flustered by small kindnesses. The humor comes from the gap between his job and his gentle hobbies. It's a sweet, relaxing read for anyone who wants a smile.
247: Night of the Living Cat by Hawkman and Mecha-Roots (Seven Seas) is a goofy horror comedy. A strange plague has spread across the world: anyone who touches a cat turns into one. Society has collapsed into a fluffy apocalypse, and the few remaining humans must resist the urge to pet, cuddle or feed the cats around them. It's a perfect pick for cat lovers and anyone who enjoys a zombie story played for laughs.
248: Dogs: Bullets & Carnage by Shirow Miwa (Viz Media) is a stylish, violent action series. In a decaying city above a mysterious underground, four very different people make their living with blades and bullets: a retired hitman, a chain-smoking freelancer, a scarred gunman and a young swordswoman searching for the man who killed her mother. Their paths slowly cross. It's a great fit for readers who like gritty, cinematic art and antiheroes.
251: Yuzu the Pet Vet by Mingo Ito (Kodansha) is a warm, kid-friendly story about caring for animals. Yuzu is an elementary school girl who loves animals and spends her time at her uncle's veterinary clinic. Each chapter brings new pets and owners with problems to solve, and Yuzu learns more about what it takes to be a vet. It's a great pick for young readers, with real tips on pet care tucked into the stories.
253: Classmates by Asumiko Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a gentle boys' love romance. Hikaru Kusakabe plays guitar in a band, and Rihito Sajo is the top student in their class. When Hikaru offers to help Rihito practice for the school chorus festival, the two boys slowly become close and fall in love. The story is soft, quiet and full of small moments. It's a lovely pick for readers who want a sweet, low-key high school romance.
256: Saturn Apartments by Hisae Iwaoka (Viz Media) is a gentle sci-fi slice-of-life story. In the far future, humanity lives in a giant ring that circles the Earth, with the rich on the upper levels and the working class below. Mitsu takes up his late father's job as a window washer on the ring's outer wall. Each chapter follows the people he meets through the glass. It's a calm, thoughtful read for fans of quiet, everyday stories.
257: From the New World by Yusuke Kishi and Toru Oikawa (Vertical) is a sci-fi mystery set a thousand years in the future. Saki Watanabe grows up in Kamisu 66, a peaceful village where people have psychokinetic powers. As she and her friends start learning to use their abilities, they begin to notice that their perfect world is hiding some very dark secrets. Readers who like dystopian mysteries with a slow-building sense of dread will enjoy it.
259: Grenadier by Sousuke Kaise (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted action story with a gentle heroine. Rushuna Tendou is a wandering gunslinger in a world at war, but she would rather end a fight with a smile than a bullet. Her goal is to disarm her enemies and win them over with kindness. Along the way she travels with Yajiro, a serious young swordsman. It's a good fit for readers who like western-style action with a soft heart.
260: Forbidden Scrollery by ZUN and Moe Harukawa (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy story set in the Touhou Project world of Gensokyo. Kosuzu Motoori is a curious girl who works at her family's book rental shop in the human village. She can read any writing, including the dangerous youkai books that come through the shop, and her curiosity keeps getting her into trouble. It's a charming pick for Touhou fans and anyone who loves book-themed stories.
262: Associate Professor Akira Takatsuki's Conjecture by Mikage Sawamura (Yen Press) is a gentle mystery light novel. Naoya Fukamachi is a college student who can hear lies, which has made him lonely. He signs up for a folklore class taught by the charming Akira Takatsuki and ends up as the professor's assistant, helping him look into urban legends and strange incidents. Readers who like low-key mysteries and odd-couple partners will enjoy it.
264: Inside Mari by Shuzo Oshimi (Denpa) is a psychological drama about identity. Isao is a lonely college dropout who spends his days gaming and secretly following a high school girl named Mari on her way home. One morning he wakes up in Mari's body, with no idea where Mari herself has gone. The story is tense, strange and thoughtful about how people see themselves. It's for older readers who like unsettling, character-driven stories.
267: Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon Eternal Edition by Naoko Takeuchi (Kodansha) is the classic magical-girl story in a larger, deluxe format. Usagi Tsukino is a crybaby middle schooler until she meets Luna, a talking cat who tells her she is the warrior Sailor Moon. Soon Usagi is fighting evil and gathering the other Sailor Guardians. It's a wonderful way for longtime fans and new readers to enjoy the series with better paper and color pages.
269: Goodnight Punpun by Inio Asano (Viz Media) is a raw, emotional coming-of-age drama. Punpun Onodera is an ordinary boy, though he's drawn as a simple cartoon bird, and the story follows him from childhood into adulthood. It begins as he falls for Aiko, a new girl at school, while his family falls apart around him. It's a moving, often heavy read for older readers who appreciate honest and experimental storytelling.
270: The Kurosagi Corpse Delivery Service by Eiji Otsuka and Housui Yamazaki (Dark Horse) is a darkly funny horror mystery. Five students at a Buddhist university can't find jobs, so they start a business using their odd talents. Kuro Karatsu can talk to the dead, and the team helps corpses finish their business, whether that means getting home or getting revenge. It's a great pick for readers who like horror mixed with humor.
275: Agents of the Four Seasons by Kana Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a beautiful fantasy light novel from the author of Violet Evergarden. In this world, the seasons are brought each year by four chosen Agents. Hinagiku, the Agent of Spring, returns after being missing for ten years, and with her loyal guard Sakura, she sets out to bring spring back to the land. It's a lyrical, emotional read for fans of gentle fantasy and strong bonds.
279: The Shiunji Family Children by Reiji Miyajima (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about a big, unusual family. Arata Shiunji has grown up as the only son among six sisters in a wealthy household. One day their father reveals that none of the siblings are related by blood, and suddenly everyone in the house sees each other differently. Fans of family comedy and harem romance will enjoy the chaos.
280: Alive: The Final Evolution by Tadashi Kawashima and Adachitoka (Del Rey) is a sci-fi thriller. A strange wave of suicides sweeps across the world, and the few survivors who resist it come away changed, with new powers. Taisuke Kanou is an ordinary high schooler whose friends are caught up in the outbreak, and he finds himself pulled into a fight to understand what's happening. It's a tense read for fans of dark sci-fi.
282: Cosmos by Ryuhei Tamura (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery with action. Kanade Mizuhara is a young man who can tell when people are lying, a gift that has made his life hard. He's recruited by Cosmos, an insurance investigation company that looks into fraud involving aliens living secretly among humans. It's a fun pick for readers who like quirky investigators and monster-of-the-week cases.
287: The World's Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country's Novice Seeker by Tôwa with illustrations by Huuka Kazabana (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Office worker Arihito Atobe dies in a bus accident and wakes in a world of labyrinths. He's given the job of Rearguard, a support class that powers up allies from behind, and he forms a party with his former boss. Fans of party-building dungeon stories will enjoy it.
289: Rozen Maiden by PEACH-PIT (Seven Seas) is a gothic fantasy drama. Jun Sakurada is a middle schooler who has shut himself in his room. One day he receives a mysterious box containing Shinku, a beautiful living doll who demands he become her servant. Soon Jun is pulled into the Alice Game, a battle between living dolls who all want to become the perfect girl. Fans of gothic fashion and dark fairy tales will love it.
295: Übel Blatt by Etorouji Shiono (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy story of revenge. Years ago, fourteen young warriors were sent to stop an invasion, and the survivors were hailed as the Seven Heroes. Now a young-looking swordsman named Köinzell travels the empire, hunting those heroes with a deadly purpose of his own. It's a grim, action-heavy series for older readers who like brutal battles and political fantasy.
296: Classroom for Heroes by Shin Araki (Yen Press) is a fantasy school comedy light novel. Blade is the hero who defeated the Demon Lord, but he has no idea how to live a normal life. To learn, he enrolls at Rostalgia Academy as an ordinary student, where his overwhelming strength and total lack of common sense cause constant trouble. It's a light, fun read for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and school antics.
298: Gods' Games We Play by Kei Sazane (Yen Press) is a fantasy light novel about high-stakes games. In this world, the gods are bored, and they challenge humans to games of wit and strategy. Fay is a young apostle with a talent for these contests, and he teams up with Leshea, a former goddess who wants to play for herself. Readers who like clever puzzles and battles of wits will have fun with it.
